description.narrative:
Fair Finance International aims to initiate a race to the top between financial institutions, and to bring about a self-reinforcing process whereby financial institutions continuously raise their standards, resulting in more sustainable lending, investments and asset management all over the world.
The overall vision of the Fair Finance International is to contribute to a just world without poverty, in which all human beings enjoy their rights within the environmental boundaries of our planet, supported by a financial sector that lives up to its responsibilities towards our societies. It is through this vision that the proposed support by Sida aims to achieve the following overall impact: to reduce poverty, safeguard human rights, preserve the environment and further achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals, linking policy change to real change in the lives of poor and marginalized people living in 11 developing countries, by engaging with financial institutions and regulators that impact these issues.

Fair Finance International syftar till att inleda ett "race to the top" mellan finansinstitut för att åstadkomma en självförstärkande process där finansinstitut kontinuerligt höjer sina ambitioner, vilket resulterar i mer hållbar utlåning, investeringar och kapitalförvaltning över hela världen.
Den övergripande visionen för Fair Finance International är att bidra till en rättvis värld utan fattigdom, där alla människor åtnjuter sina rättigheter inom miljögränserna på vår planet, stödda av en finansiell sektor som lever upp till sitt ansvar gentemot våra samhällen. Det är genom denna vision som Sidas föreslagna stöd syftar till att uppnå följande övergripande effekter: att minska fattigdom, skydda mänskliga rättigheter, bevara miljön och och att nå målen för hållbar utveckling (SDG), koppla policy förändring till förändring i livet för fattiga och marginaliserade människor som bor i 11 utvecklingsländer genom att samarbeta med finansinstitutioner och tillsynsmyndigheter som påverkar dessa frågor.

The overall vision of the Fair Finance International is to contribute to a just world without poverty, in which all human beings enjoy their rights within the environmental boundaries of our planet, supported by a financial sector that lives up to its responsibilities towards our societies. It is through this vision that the proposed support by Sida aims to achieve the following overall impact: to reduce poverty, safeguard human rights, preserve the environment and further achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), linking policy change to real change in the lives of poor and marginalized people living in 11 developing countries, by engaging with financial institutions and regulators that impact these issues.

Fair Finance International (FFI) seeks to strengthen the commitment of banks and other financial institutions to act on and adhere to social, environmental, and human rights standards. FFl underlines the importance of its work to strengthen of the capacity of civil society organisations and alliance building to effectively influence the financial sector and regulators.
The Fair Finance network currently consists of a number of country coalitions comprised of more than 100 partner organizations.
The cooperation partner reports that its coalitions have contributed to improved policies, practices and commitments by large financial sector actors. More specifically, FFI coalitions partners contributed to improvements in national regulation.
The cooperation reports that it continues strengthening civil society in developing countries to increase the impact of a movement that demands a fair and green financial sector. Fair Finance methodology an assessment tool plays important role not only in scrutinizing but also influencing the financial sector through dialogue on the outcome of assessment.
In 2022, the FFI network registered a total of 305 improvements to financial institutions' policies in both developed and developing countries.
More than 2.85 million people were reached through physical and online activities by the FFI network in 2022, of which more than 43,000 people acted/engaged for an inclusive financial sector.
The Fair Finance Guide International (FFGI methodology) as an assessment tool plays an important role not only in reviewing but also in influencing the financial sector through dialogue around the results of the assessment. According to an endline evaluation during 2023 an overall improvement in ESG policies is confirmed in countries where the FFGI methodology is used. This is considered to have led to a "race to the top" among financiers.
In 2023, FFI conducted a major investigation of the mining company Glencore's operations in Latin America which was followed by campaigns in Europe. FFI provided recommendations on how Glencore could bring its operations in line with its international commitments. The investigation resulted in dialogue with Glencore on a number of areas for improvement.
